summary: Unpinned GitHub dependency pulls libsignal from a personal repo's mutable HEAD
details: package.json declares the libsignal dependency as `github:tenka-san/libsignal-node` with no commit SHA or tag. On `npm install`, npm clones whatever bytes currently sit at that personal GitHub repository's default-branch HEAD and installs them into the dependency tree, running any lifecycle scripts the fetched payload defines. There is no version pin, no integrity check, and the source is a non-registry, personal-account repository under third-party control — whoever controls tenka-san/libsignal-node can substitute arbitrary code at any time, and every subsequent install of @rizzkezik/bailseys will execute it. The project is a Baileys (WhatsApp library) fork; libsignal is a core cryptographic dependency normally sourced from a pinned registry release, so an unpinned mutable git reference in that slot is a direct install-time code-inclusion path from an untrusted control sphere.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
